newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies close mixed, yen resumes declines.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies close mixed, yen resumes declines.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed in a lackluster trading session, with yen contracts resuming their declines, traders and analysts said.
"There was renewed yen weakness on the crosses after dollar/yen failed to take out the 113.00 spot level," Lisa Finstrom, a currency analyst at Smith Barney, said.

December yen set a daily high at $0.008897, as the dollar/yen spot level fell to 113.00. However, dollar/yen failed to fall below that support zone, and encouraged speculators to drive the spot level higher due to technical and momentum indicators.
"We are going to stay in this broad range between 113.00 and 114.00 for awhile," one floor trader said, as December yen fell to the 114.00 spot equivalent of $0.008822.
Several analysts noted that a wire service reported a projections by a former foreign government official that the dollar/yen could drop to the 100.00 to 110.00 area.
One trader said two firms bought a total of 2,000 December yen contracts after that story was released, but the market found little upside momentum.

Sterling futures remained higher throughout the session, with December hitting at contract hight at $1.6460. Traders said funds were willing to buy the currency on dips on ideas that regulatory authorities may delay the actual merger of British Telecom and MCI Communications.
In addition, traders said the bullish sterling/yen trend was still intact, as investors moved into high-yielding currencies overall.
The mark also strengthened against the yen, and helped weaken the dollar against the mark. December marks rallied slightly in thin trade.
Meanwhile, peso futures were sharply higher, with December extending gains above the critical resistance level of $0.122900.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was down $0.000041 at $0.008833, marks were up $0.0016 at $0.6637, Swiss francs were up $0.0019 at $0.7927, sterling was $0.0106 higher at a contract settlement high of $1.6444, Canadian dollars were down $0.0009 at $0.7507, Australian dollars lost $0.0026 at $0.7860 and Mexican pesos were $0.000700 at $0.123200. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
